title: Genesis Launches Hybrids at the LA Auto Show, EREV Coming in 2027
summary:
Korean luxury automaker Genesis launched its first hybrid models this week, debuting new powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show.
More efficient, more powerfulThe G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain.
Genesis hasn’t announced official fuel economy estimates, but says the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient.
Familiar designAside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts.
Like the standard models, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids feature a large 27-inch OLED display.

title: MacBook Neo Could Get New Colors and Upgrades Every Year
summary:
Apple has put the MacBook Neo on an annual update cycle matching the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
Writing in his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman said the next model is code-named J701 and due next spring.
Both are previously rumored upgrades.
Color options have been rumored before, but Gurman said Apple plans to refresh the $699 Neo's colors frequently, adding "we'll see if that trend starts with the first follow-up."
The annual cycle will target the low end of the Windows PC and Chromebook markets.

title: CrowdStrike is spending $43.9 billion to buy Zscaler in a huge cybersecurity deal as tech outages spread
summary:
With tech outages ripping across the world, CrowdStrike (CRWD) is shelling out big-time money to acquire fellow cybersecurity player and longtime partner Zscaler (ZS).
The two will also combine businesses led by two veteran tech founders: George Kurtz at CrowdStrike and Jay Chaudhry at Zscaler.
CrowdStrike will spend $43.9 billion to buy Zscaler, it said on Monday.
CrowdStrike said it expects revenue synergies to build progressively over the first 30 months following an expected close in mid 2027, reaching about $1 billion in annualized run-rate revenue synergies by the end of that period.
"We view this as the clearest signal yet that cybersecurity is consolidating into a handful of platforms, with the AI era forcing the hand of vendors who had been content to partner," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

title: Accounting firms are racing to use AI. Most still lack the infrastructure to make it work, according to a new report.
summary:
Wolters Kluwer Tax & Accounting sells software and tools to tax, accounting, and audit firms.
On that measure, accounting firms are moving quickly: 88% of US professionals said they use generative AI for daily work, and 68% said the same for agentic AI.
What US accounting firms aren't achieving is a sophisticated tech infrastructure to back up their appetite for the new technology, according to the study.
Senior executives tend to say that the shift makes accounting work more exciting and people-focused.
Ensuring big operational change, rather than simply adding AI tools to existing processes, is the next challenge, the report said.

summary:

title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
summary:
Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.
The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him.
On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement.
The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support.

title: AI is being used to clone real people's videos
summary:
Is this real or AI?
It is a question increasingly asked underneath social media videos, and often difficult to tell.
Across social media, AI-generated characters are appearing in videos that look remarkably similar to those posted by real people.
Experts call the practice "reskinning" and say it is made possible by cheap, easy-to-use AI tools.
Others appear to be experimenting with AI to make people laugh or simply for the attention that comes with going viral.

title: Apple Explores Using Light to Move Data Between Server Chips
summary:
Apple is hiring an engineering program manager to work on light-based data connections for its server chips, in what could be a sign of the company's broader ambitions in data-center infrastructure.
The Silicon Photonics EPM listing was highlighted by Korea's Maeil Business, and seeks experience with optical I/O, silicon photonics and co-packaged optics, with responsibilities spanning concept through mass production.
The optical interconnects are considered to be an emerging core technology for AI data centers, and use light to move data between chips rather than to perform computations.
The listing follows a September report that Apple was exploring a return to the server market using its own M-series chips amid cost and speed challenges.
Apple discontinued Xserve in 2011.

summary:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO.

I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO.
